context.title: The King Enters Jerusalem
context.summary: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey to shouts of 'Hosanna', clears the temple, curses a fruitless fig tree, and answers a challenge to his authority with parables of two sons and wicked vineyard tenants.
context.background: Jerusalem swelled with pilgrims at Passover. Jesus rides a donkey, not a war horse, fulfilling Zechariah's picture of a humble king. Pilgrims needed approved coins and sacrificial animals, and that trade had moved into the temple courts.

customs.note: Hebrew for 'save, please', from Psalm 118:25. By Jesus' day it had become a festival shout of praise.
Owners guarded vineyards with a hedge and a watchtower. The details echo Isaiah's song of the vineyard, a picture of Israel.

watchFor: Jesus quotes Isaiah and Jeremiah: 'house of prayer… den of thieves' (v. 13).
Children in the temple shout what the leaders refuse to say (vv. 15–16).
The rejected stone becomes the head of the corner (v. 42).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

places.name: Bethphage
places.summary: House of the unripe fig, a village on the Mount of Olives, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho (Matt. 21:1; Mark 11:1; Luke 19:29), and very close to Bethany.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: mount of Olives
places.summary: So called from the olive trees with which its sides are clothed, is a mountain ridge on the east of Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:7; Ezek. 11:23; Zech. 14:4), from which it is separated by the valley of Kidron.

places.name: Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

places.name: Bethany
places.summary: A village on the south-eastern slope of the Mount of Olives (Mark 11:1), about 2 miles east of Jerusalem, on the road to Jericho. It derived its name from the number of palm-trees which grew there.

events.title: Holy Week
